heterogeneity.DIRECTION_TEST: NOT APPLICABLE -- I-squared is 0.0%, below the threshold at which the direction test is informative. The trials are consistent with a common effect and no heterogeneity caution is warranted. Applying one here would manufacture doubt the data do not support, which is the mirror failure of ignoring heterogeneity that matters.
heterogeneity.how_to_read_this_at_low_k: At k=2 or k=3 these statistics are weak evidence about consistency in EITHER direction. A low value means the estimates are CONSISTENT WITH a common effect, not that one is demonstrated.
heterogeneity.tau2_estimator: REML -- copied from this block's declared `estimator`, which is the authoritative record of how the pool was computed. NOT inferred: an object that declared no estimator would be left undeclared here, because the absence is itself the finding.
heterogeneity.i2_definition: UNDECIDABLE from this object. Recorded as undecidable rather than guessed.

primary.WHAT_THIS_POOL_IS_AND_IS_NOT: THIS IS NOT A POOL OF THE FIVE TRIALS THIS PAGE SEEDS. It is the DAPIVIRINE VAGINAL RING pair, which is the only subset sharing an intervention and a comparator. The page seeds five trials testing FOUR DIFFERENT THINGS: oral Truvada against placebo (NCT00625404, 33/1024 vs 35/1032), tenofovir 1% VAGINAL GEL against placebo gel (NCT00705679, 61/996 vs 70/996), the dapivirine ring against a placebo ring (the two pooled here), and NCT01386294 which posts NO RESULTS. Oral tablet, microbicide gel and vaginal ring are different interventions with different delivery, adherence and mechanism. POOLING ALL FIVE WOULD BE A CLASS CLAIM THE PAGE'S DATA CANNOT SUPPORT.
primary.the_person_years_primary_CHECKED: NCT00705679's registered primary 'Person-years of Follow-up' is NOT an effect measure, and that was flagged before reading. IT IS ONE OF TWO PRIMARIES: the same trial also registers 'Number of HIV-1 Infections' and posts 61/996 against 70/996. So the concern was real but not disqualifying -- the trial does register a usable endpoint. IT IS STILL NOT IN THIS POOL, because its INTERVENTION is a vaginal gel and not the ring.

published_synthesis_comparison.what_is_owed: No published synthesis of the two dapivirine ring trials has been read.

primary.what_this_does_not_establish: NOT that dapivirine ring PrEP works or does not work in this population -- NO RISK-OF-BIAS ASSESSMENT IS RECORDED and adherence, which dominates ring effectiveness, is not an outcome here. NOT anything about oral or gel PrEP, which are excluded above. NOT that the three excluded trials are poor: they answer different questions. NOT reliability at k=2 -- see Hartung-Knapp.

house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.estimator: REML with Hartung-Knapp, t on k-1 = 1 degree(s) of freedom (t = 12.7062)
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.THE_POINT_ESTIMATE_IS_UNCHANGED: The published point is 0.7030 and the house-rule point is 0.7030. THE NUMBER A READER REMEMBERS DOES NOT MOVE; what differs is the precision claim. That is why nothing downstream catches this -- every memorable quantity survives.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.variance_inflation_floor: A FLOOR OF 1 IS APPLIED TO THE VARIANCE-INFLATION FACTOR so the adjustment can never NARROW an interval below the unadjusted one. That guard is the recognised modification for exactly this instability, and its existence is evidence the small-k behaviour is a KNOWN problem with KNOWN handling rather than a novel judgement.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.no_rule_is_decided_here: The house rule is REML with Hartung-Knapp below k=10, settled days ago. Whether it means ALWAYS or WITH A FLOOR AT k=3 is a decision about this corpus, not a computation, and it has been referred rather than taken. BOTH INTERVALS STAND ON THIS PAGE UNTIL IT IS MADE. Nothing is unpublished and no reader is left with only the narrower one.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.what_this_means_for_this_pool: THE PUBLISHED INTERVAL EXCLUDES 1 AND THE HOUSE-RULE INTERVAL CROSSES IT. A SIGNIFICANCE VERDICT TURNS ON THE INTERVAL METHOD ALONE. A reader shown only the published interval has been told something firmer than the evidence supports; a reader shown only the wider one loses that the contributing trials agree. BOTH ARE HERE.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.read_the_width_with_care: AT k=2 HARTUNG-KNAPP USES t ON ONE DEGREE OF FREEDOM -- 12.7062 against the normal 1.9600 -- and the interval is enormously wider. That width is a property of the method at very few studies, not a measurement of this evidence. It is recorded so a reader can see it; it is NOT presented as the better interval.

POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.a_eligibility_not_enrollment_for_under_1: READ THIS BESIDE THE ESTIMATE. This review is named for ADOLESCENT GIRLS AND YOUNG WOMEN. BOTH CONTRIBUTING REGISTRATIONS SET A MINIMUM ELIGIBILITY AGE OF 18 YEARS -- NCT01539226 and NCT01617096, both FEMALE, both 18 to 45 years. THE OBJECT DOES NOT HOLD ENROLLED-AGE DISTRIBUTIONS, so it cannot say whether any adolescent was actually enrolled. The estimate does not speak to people under 18 as an eligibility group, and GRADE indirectness is rated down for that reason.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.b_the_countries_are_right_even_though_th: Stated so the caution is not read wider than it is. The Ring Study ran in South Africa and Uganda; ASPIRE ran in Malawi, South Africa, Uganda and Zimbabwe. BY REGION THIS IS DIRECTLY THE POPULATION OF INTEREST. The indirectness is about AGE ALONE.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.c_the_effect_does_not_survive_the_small_: The unadjusted interval is RR 0.7030 (0.5660 to 0.8731) and EXCLUDES no difference. This project's Hartung-Knapp interval at k = 2 is 0.1725 to 2.8655 -- and NOT 0.4054 to 1.2191, which is metafor's RAW unfloored knha interval and was misattributed to this project in the first version of this note and INCLUDES it. THE HONEST READING OF THAT IS NARROW: at k = 2 the t critical value is 12.7062 and almost nothing survives the adjustment, so this is much weaker evidence against the result than the same disagreement would be at larger k. It is disclosed because a reader is entitled to both intervals, not because it overturns the estimate.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.d_no_external_check_exists_for_this_esti: A screen of eight records found NO published synthesis pooling HIV seroconversion across these two trials -- the five flagged syntheses are about adherence, acceptability and pregnancy outcomes. THIS ESTIMATE IS UNREPLICATED so far as this project has looked.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.e_a_registered_safety_co_primary_is_not_: Both registrations register adverse events as a SECOND PRIMARY OUTCOME. This review carries only the efficacy primary. That is a scope fact, not a defect in the estimate, and it is recorded so a reader does not read this page as a benefit-and-harm summary.

estimand_mismatch.trials_analysed: time to event, with censoring and unequal follow-up
estimand_mismatch.statement: ⚠️ THE QUANTITY POOLED HERE IS NOT THE QUANTITY THE TRIALS ANALYSED. Both trials analysed HIV-1 acquisition as TIME TO EVENT, with censoring and unequal follow-up; ASPIRE reports a median of 1.6 years per participant and a follow-up window of 12 to 14 months on its registered primary outcome. What this review pools is a RISK RATIO over binary counts, because binary counts are what the object holds. That is a different quantity from the trials' own estimand: it weights a participant followed for two years the same as one followed for twelve months, and it will differ from a hazard ratio whenever follow-up differs between arms. It is reported because it is what the evidence here supports, and it is labelled rather than presented as though it were the trials' own analysis.
estimand_mismatch.source_quote: ASPIRE, registered primary outcome time frame: “minimum of 12 months and a maximum of 14 months per participant”. The Ring Study: “24 months”.
estimand_mismatch.what_would_fix_it: Per-arm person-time or the trials' own hazard ratios with their standard errors. Neither is in this object; neither has been extracted; and no hazard ratio is derived here from counts, because a hazard ratio derived from binary counts is a risk ratio wearing a different name.

subgroups_interaction.applies_to: the PRESPECIFIED split (under 25 versus 25 and over)
subgroups_interaction.verbatim: However, the efficacy of HIV-1 protection differed significantly according to age, with an efficacy of 61% (95% CI, 32 to 77; P<0.001) among women 25 years of age or older and 10% (95% CI, −41 to 43; P = 0.64) among those under the age of 25 years (P = 0.02 for interaction).
subgroups_interaction.how_to_read_it: ⚠️ AN INTERACTION TEST STRENGTHENS A POST-HOC SUBGROUP; IT DOES NOT MAKE IT PRESPECIFIED. P = 0.02 is reported for the PRESPECIFIED age split, and the age-categorised thirds below it remain POST HOC. Both facts must be read together: presenting the thirds as a finding because an interaction test exists would recreate exactly the overclaim this review caught in its own reference -- a post-hoc subgroup presented as a finding.

primary.subgroup_footnote: Two of these strata are PRESPECIFIED (under 25 versus 25 and over) and two are POST HOC; each row says which. For the prespecified split the trial reports P = 0.02 for interaction, applying to the PRESPECIFIED split (under 25 versus 25 and over). That test strengthens the prespecified split — it does NOT make the post-hoc strata prespecified, and no interaction test is reported for them. The source's words: “However, the efficacy of HIV-1 protection differed significantly according to age, with an efficacy of 61% (95% CI, 32 to 77; P<0.001) among women 25 years of age or older and 10% (95% CI, −41 to 43; P = 0.64) among those under the age of 25 years (P = 0.02 for interaction).” These strata are reported, not tested against one another beyond that single interaction test.

resolved_2026_08_21.the_text_that_decides_it: RoB 2 guidance 2019, Box 4, signalling question 1.1: "Answer 'No information' if the only information about randomization methods is a statement that the study is randomized." And section 4.4: "A judgement of low risk of bias requires that the trial has an adequate method of concealing the allocation sequence from those involved in enrolling participants, and there are no concerns about generation of the allocation sequence." Cochrane Handbook 6.5 section 8.3 names the domain's three components.
resolved_2026_08_21.why_this_is_not_an_adjudicated_dispute: A blind second assessor from a different model family disagreed with this domain on 89% of judgements across 22 topics. THAT WOULD ORDINARILY BE A DISPUTE TO ADJUDICATE. It is not one: the tool's own text names this exact evidential situation -- a bare statement that a study was randomised -- and prescribes the answer. The second assessor is not being deferred to; the guidance is being applied.
resolved_2026_08_21.what_the_registry_gives_and_does_not: A ClinicalTrials.gov design module records `allocation: RANDOMIZED`. It carries no sequence-generation method and no allocation-concealment mechanism. The original judgement's own note said so before scoring LOW.
resolved_2026_08_21.how_this_maps_to_the_tool_s_algorithm: The tool maps 'No information' on 1.1 and 1.2 with no baseline concern to a DOMAIN judgement of SOME CONCERNS. This project writes NO_INFORMATION on the domain when it could not be judged from the sources read, and caps the OVERALL at SOME_CONCERNS. Same place, and it keeps 'we could not judge this' distinguishable from 'we judged it and had concerns'.
resolved_2026_08_21.what_does_not_change: NO OVERALL RATING AND NO GRADE CERTAINTY MOVES. All 51 judgements were already capped at SOME_CONCERNS or HIGH by another NO_INFORMATION domain.
resolved_2026_08_21.what_would_close_it_properly: The trial publications or protocols, which carry sequence generation and concealment. Neither was read. Until one is, LOW is not available on this domain for any result in this corpus.

steps.reason: Both results are SOME_CONCERNS. D1, D4 and D5 are LOW on read registrations, but D2 and D3 are NO_INFORMATION and on a PrEP trial those are the adherence and attrition domains -- the ones that decide whether an intention-to-treat ring effect reflects the drug or its use.

tau-squared is EXACTLY ZERO, Q 0.1535 on 1 df, p = 0.6952, I-squared 0.00%. The two intervals -- 0.6711 (0.4884 to 0.9221) and 0.7320 (0.5442 to 0.9845) -- agree in size and in conclusion. Downgrading here would manufacture a caution the numbers do not support.

THIS TOPIC IS NAMED FOR ADOLESCENT GIRLS AND YOUNG WOMEN. Both registrations set a MINIMUM ELIGIBILITY AGE OF 18 YEARS (NCT01539226 and NCT01617096, eligibility module, both 18 to 45 years, FEMALE). The object DOES NOT HOLD ENROLLED-AGE DISTRIBUTIONS, so it cannot say whether any adolescent was actually enrolled. The estimate is therefore indirect for people under 18 in the named population, in whom adherence to a vaginal ring is the very thing in question. THE SETTING IS NOT THE PROBLEM: the trials ran in South Africa, Uganda, Malawi and Zimbabwe, which is directly the population of interest by region.

steps.move: LOW to VERY LOW -- WARRANTED AND NOT APPLIED, see reason
steps.reason: k = 2. The Hartung-Knapp interval is RR 0.7030 (0.1725 to 2.8655) on t = 12.7062 with 1 df AND IT INCLUDES NO DIFFERENCE, where the unadjusted interval excludes it. A downgrade is warranted on that alone. IT IS NOT APPLIED, and the reason is stated rather than hidden: at k = 2 the t critical value is 12.7062 and ONLY A VERY LARGE EFFECT SURVIVES HARTUNG-KNAPP AT ALL, so the adjusted interval at this k is weak evidence of imprecision in either direction. The rating is left at LOW and the disagreement is disclosed to the reader instead.
k = 2. A funnel plot and its asymmetry tests have essentially no power below about ten trials (Handbook 13.3.5.4), so this is NOT ASSESSABLE rather than 'undetected'.

One query on one database was run and no included-study table was opened anywhere. manuscript.introduction:
This review asks: Does a dapivirine vaginal ring reduce HIV-1 seroconversion compared with a placebo vaginal ring in women?

It pools 2 randomised trials, against placebo vaginal ring.

The outcome pooled is HIV-1 seroconversion.

Every count and denominator behind those estimates is read as follows. REGISTRY THROUGHOUT. Counts and denominators read from ClinicalTrials.gov posted results.
